The first half was lovely, but past the twenty mile marker their legs turned to concrete, and the last six miles were a walk-shuffle-walk beside a woman in a frog hat having the same day; they finished eleven seconds apart and hugged like family. They say they went out too fast, that it was on them, and that they don't usually let anyone see them struggle, so doing so in front of thousands was its own kind of finish line. They are prouder of the walking than of the running, and are keeping the entry to read the night before the next start line and start slower. It was a mixed day, and they will decide what they think about it tomorrow.
